title: Air India Warns of US Flight Delays After FAA Ground Stop Snarls Departures Nationwide
excerpt: A telecommunications outage forced the FAA to halt US departures on Friday. The ground stop has since been lifted, but Air India says consequential disruption to its US flights is possible and passengers should check their flight status before leaving for the airport.
body:
• The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop on Friday after a telecommunications outage hit air traffic control operations, affecting all 22 regional air route traffic control centres. The stop has since been lifted, but delays and cancellations are expected to continue.
  • Air India advised passengers on Saturday that departures across the US are impacted, with possible consequential disruption to its flights to and from the US, and asked travellers to check the latest status of their flights before heading to the airport.
  • FlightAware reported more than 10,000 delays and more than 4,000 cancellations during the disruption, according to reports — roughly two weeks before the Thanksgiving holiday.
  • If you are flying Air India to or from the US this weekend, check your flight before you leave home: go to airindia.com, open 'Book & Manage' and then 'Flight Status', and enter your flight number, PNR or route and date of travel.

Air India has warned passengers that its flights to and from the United States may be delayed after a communications outage forced US aviation authorities to halt departures nationwide on Friday, in one of the most sweeping disruptions to American air travel in years.

'A nationwide ground stop is currently in effect across the US due to communication outages affecting air traffic operations. As a result, departures from airports across US are impacted, with possible consequential disruptions to Air India flights to and from the US,' the airline said in a statement posted on X. 'Passengers are advised to check the latest status of their flights and plan their journey to the airport accordingly. Our teams continue to closely monitor the situation and will share updates as available.'

What happened

The FAA announced the ground stop on Friday afternoon, local time, after a temporary telecommunications outage affected air traffic control operations. The disruption affected all 22 regional air route traffic control centres, which manage aircraft travelling between airports, and the agency said the decision was taken 'due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety'.

A ground stop holds aircraft at their departure airports. Flights already in the air were allowed to continue to their destinations and land, with inbound international flights handled on a case-by-case basis. According to Reuters, the ground stop was later lifted, although delays and knock-on disruption were expected to continue as airlines worked through the backlog. FlightAware reported more than 10,000 delays and more than 4,000 cancellations in the hours after the disruption began, according to reports, and at least 600 flights were diverted.

Bloomberg reported that flights were halted nationwide for the longest time since the September 11, 2001 attacks. Reports describe it as only the third nationwide ground stop in US history, after 9/11 and a January 2023 failure of an FAA system.

What officials say caused it

The exact cause of the outage had not been established. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said FAA technicians were investigating the failure. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters that officials had acted as a precaution following a telecommunications outage affecting the FAA. 'There is no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack,' he said. An airline source cited by CNN said the FAA had told carriers that a network router problem may have triggered the disruption, reportedly first noticed at Chicago Midway International Airport — that account has not been officially confirmed.

American Airlines said some flights at certain airports began receiving clearance to depart as restrictions eased, while warning that most departures remained paused for a time and that further disruption, including unavoidable cancellations, was expected.

What Air India passengers should do

Air India's advice is to verify your flight status before travelling to the airport, and to plan your journey around the latest update rather than your original schedule. On the airline's official site, open airindia.com and select 'Book & Manage', then 'Flight Status', and enter your flight number, PNR or route along with the date of travel to see the current status. The airline said it will share further updates as they become available.

Air India operates nonstop services linking US gateways including New York, Newark, San Francisco, Chicago and Washington with Delhi and Mumbai, so weekend departures in both directions — and onward connections in India — are the ones most exposed to knock-on delays while US operations clear the backlog.
